name: Reflection, sound, ultrasound and seismic waves

terms.definition: Waves bounce off a boundary; angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. Waves may also be absorbed or transmitted.

terms.definition: Longitudinal waves that travel through solids, liquids and gases; the human range is about 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

terms.definition: Sound with a frequency higher than humans can hear (above 20 kHz); partially reflected at boundaries between materials.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. Used for medical and industrial imaging.

terms.definition: Earthquake waves: P-waves are longitudinal and travel through solids and liquids; S-waves are transverse and cannot pass through liquids.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. They are evidence for the Earth's liquid outer core.

terms.definition: Using pulses of high-frequency sound to find the depth of water.
terms.examiner: Separate Physics. Halve the time for the one-way distance.
